'''Naoki Saito''' is an [[applied mathematician]] specializing in applied and computational [[harmonic analysis]], and interested in [[feature extraction]], [[pattern recognition]], graph signal processing, [[Signal processing#Statistical|statistical signal processing]], [[Laplace operator#Spectral theory|Laplacian eigenfunctions]], and human and [[machine perception]].

==Education==
Saito studied at the [[University of Tokyo]], receiving his BEng in 1982 and his MEng in 1984. He joined Nippon [[Schlumberger]] K.K. in 1984, and in 1986 moved to Schlumberger-[[Henri George Doll|Doll]] Research (SDR), [[Ridgefield, Connecticut]], where he was a research scientist. He continued his studies, receiving his PhD in [[applied mathematics]]  from [[Yale University]] in 1994.

==Career==
Saito began teaching at the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Davis]] in 1997, where he is currently a distinguished professor and a director of the UC Davis TETRAPODS Institute of [[Data science|Data Science]],<ref>{{cite web |title=New $1.5M Institute Will Harness the Data Revolution |url=https://lettersandscience.ucdavis.edu/news/new-15m-institute-will-harness-data-revolution |website=UC Davis College of Letters and Science |date=7 October 2019 |access-date=27 February 2022}}</ref> one of [[National Science Foundation]]'s Transdisciplinary Research In Principles Of Data Science (TRIPODS) Institutes, which brings together the theoretical computer science, electrical engineering, mathematics, and statistics communities to develop the theoretical foundations of data science. He was also Chair of the Graduate Group in Applied Mathematics at UC Davis from 2007 to 2012.<ref name="ieee biography">{{cite web |title=Naoki Saito biography |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37359513900 |website=[[IEEE]] |access-date=28 February 2022}}</ref> He is a senior member of [[IEEE]] as well as a member of [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics|IMS]], [[SIAM]], and [[JSIAM]].

He served as Chair of the SIAM Activity Group on Imaging Science from 2013 to 2015, and is a member of the editorial board of ''Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis'', ''Inverse Problems and Imaging'', and ''Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision''.<ref name="ieee biography"/>

Saito received the Best Paper Awards from the [[SPIE]] (1994), and [[JSIAM]] (2016)<ref>{{cite web |title=LAURELS: Jack Gunion to Receive Sakurai Prize in Physics |url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/laurels-jack-gunion-receive-sakurai-prize-physics |website=UC Davis |date=24 October 2016 |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref> as well as the [[Henri George Doll|Henri Doll]] Award from [[Schlumberger]] (1997), Young Investigator Award from the [[Office of Naval Research|ONR]] (2000),<ref>{{cite web |title=Naoki Saito |url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/naoki-saito-0 |website=UC Davis |date=13 June 2000 |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref> and the [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]] (PECASE) (2000).<ref name="ieee biography"/>

Saito has contributed to a number of notable interdisciplinary projects including the development of a noninvasive fetal oxygen monitor<ref>{{cite web |title=Noninvasive Fetal Oxygen Monitor Could Make for Safer Deliveries |url=https://www.ucdavis.edu/news/noninvasive-fetal-oxygen-monitor-could-make-safer-deliveries |website=UC Davis |date=17 June 2020 |access-date=16 April 2022}}</ref> as well as the [[Lake Tahoe]] [[Sonification]] Project in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lake Tahoe Sonification Projection uses weather data to create artistic soundscape |url=https://www.davisenterprise.com/feature/arts/lake-tahoe-sonification-projection-uses-weather-data-to-create-artistic-soundscape-based-on-nature/ |publisher=Davis Enterprise |date=13 October 2014 |access-date=12 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Cyclical Voices of Lake Tahoe |url=https://dhi.ucdavis.edu/news/cyclical-voices-lake-tahoe |website=UC Davis Humanities Institute |date=12 May 2014 |access-date=16 April 2022}}</ref>
